Al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from him also concerning ﴿And do not confer favor seeking more﴾ that he said: "Do not give a man a gift hoping that he will give you more than it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from him also concerning ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾ that he said: "The Horn." ﴿It will be a difficult day﴾: "Severe."

Ibn Mardawayh related from him also concerning ﴿Leave me with whom I created alone﴾ that he said: "Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from him also: "That al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he recited the Qur'an to him, so it seemed he softened to it. This reached Abu Jahl, so he came to him and said: 'O uncle, your people want to gather wealth for you to give to you, for you came to Muhammad to oppose what he received.' He said: 'Quraysh know that I am among the most wealthy of them.' He said: 'Then say about him a saying by which your people will learn that you deny it and that you hate it.' He said: 'And what should I say? By Allah, there is not among you a man more knowledgeable of poetry than I, neither of its rajaz nor its qasida, nor of the poetry of the jinn. By Allah, what he says does not resemble any of this at all. By Allah, his saying has a sweetness, and it has a radiance, and it is fruitful at its top and abundant at its base, and it rises and nothing rises above it, and it breaks what is beneath it.' He said: 'By Allah, your people will not be pleased until you say something about him.' He said: 'Leave me until I reflect.' When he reflected he said: 'This is magic that is transmitted; he takes it from others.' So there was revealed ﴿Leave me with whom I created alone﴾."

'Abd al-Razzaq related this from 'Ikrimah as a mursal (a report with a missing companion in the chain), and likewise Ibn Jarir, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and others related it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he was asked about His saying ﴿And I made for him abundant wealth﴾ and he said: "The produce of one month after another month."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And I made for him abundant wealth﴾ that he said: "A thousand dinars."

Hannad related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri concerning His saying ﴿I will force him to a steep ascent﴾ that he said: "It is a mountain in the Fire; they are commanded to climb it, and whenever they place their hands upon it, it melts, and when they lift them, it returns as it was."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿stubborn﴾ that he said: "Denying."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi related from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The steep ascent (al-su'ud) is a mountain in the Fire; the disbeliever climbs it for seventy autumns, then he falls down, and he remains like that in it forever."

Al-Tirmidhi said after relating it: "It is strange; we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah from Darraj."

Ibn Kathir said: "In it there is strangeness and irregularity." End of quote. It was related by a group of people as the saying of Abu Sa'id. Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "'Su'ud' is a rock in Jahannam over which the disbeliever is dragged on his face."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him: "A mountain in the Fire."

Ibn al-Mundhir also related from him concerning His saying ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾ that he said: "It leaves none of them anything. And when they are given another creation, it does not leave them to return to the first punishment."

'Abd ibn Humayd related from him also ﴿Scorching to the human being﴾: "It scorches the skin and burns it and changes its color, so it becomes blacker than the night."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also ﴿Scorching﴾: "Burning."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th related from al-Bara': that a group of Jews asked some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) about the guardians of Jahannam. He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Then Jibril came and informed the Prophet (ﷺ), and at that moment there was revealed to him ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 74, verses 31–37:

When the words of the Most High were revealed, ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾, Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad have no helpers except nineteen? Muhammad frightens you with nineteen, while you are the numerous ones (al-duhm). Would each hundred men among you be unable to overpower one of them and then get out of the Fire?" Then Abu al-Ashadd, a man of the Banu Jumah, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, when the Day of Resurrection comes, I will walk in front of you and push ten of them with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and then we will go on and enter Paradise." So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, meaning: We have not made those who manage the affairs of the Fire and who carry out the punishment of its inhabitants anything except angels (p-1554). So who can withstand the angels, and who can overpower them? How, then, do you disbelievers attempt to contend with them?

It was also said that He made them angels because they are of a different kind from the created beings of jinn and humans, so they are not affected by the tenderness and compassion that affect gatherings of people. And it was said that it is because they are the most upright of God's creation in His right and in being angry for Him, and the strongest of them in might and the most powerful in seizing. ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial﴾, that is, a misguidance for those who considered their number small, and a tribulation for them. The meaning is: We have not made their number this number mentioned in the Qur'an except as a misguidance and a tribulation for them, so that they said what they said, in order that their punishment would be doubled and God's anger against them would increase.

It was also said that the meaning of ﴿except as a trial﴾ is except as a punishment, as in His words: ﴿On the Day they will be burned over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], that is, they will be punished. The lam in His words ﴿that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾ is connected to "We made". By "the People of the Scripture" is meant the Jews and the Christians, because what was revealed in the Qur'an agrees with what is in their possession, namely that the number of the guardians of Hell is nineteen. This was said by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Mujahid and others. The meaning is that Allah made the number of the guardians this number so that certainty would be attained by the Jews and the Christians regarding the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), because the Qur'an agrees with what is in their books. ﴿And those who believed may increase in faith﴾. It was said that by "those who believed" is meant those among the People of the Scripture who believed, such as Abd Allah ibn Salam. It was also said that he meant by "those who believed" the believers of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The meaning is: that they may increase in certainty upon their certainty, when they saw the agreement of the People of the Scripture with them. The clause ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾ confirms what preceded concerning certainty and the increase of faith. The meaning is the negation of doubt about them in the religion, or about the fact that the number of the guardians of Hell is nineteen. In reality there is no doubt among the believers, but this is by way of indirect address to others, those in whose hearts there is doubt. ﴿And so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ By "those in whose hearts is disease" are meant the hypocrites. Although the surah is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy at that time, this is a report of what would happen in Medina. Or the disease means merely the occurrence of doubt and uncertainty, which exists among the disbelievers.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, so the disease in this verse is the disagreement. By "and the disbelievers" is meant the disbelievers of the Arabs from the people of Mecca and others. The meaning of ﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾ is: what did He intend by this astonishing number, being astonishing like a parable.

Al-Layth said: "Mathal" means a statement (hadith), and from it is His word: ﴿The example of Paradise which the God-fearing have been promised﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35], that is, its description is the report about it. ﴿Thus Allah leaves astray whom He wills﴾, that is, like that misguidance mentioned before, which is His word: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved﴾. ﴿Allah leaves astray whom He wills﴾ from among His servants. The kaf is an adjective (na't) of an omitted verbal noun (masdar). ﴿And guides whom He wills﴾ from among His servants. The meaning is: like that misguidance for the disbelievers and that guidance for the believers, Allah leaves astray whom He wills to be misguided and guides whom He wills to be guided.

It was also said that the meaning is: thus Allah leaves astray from Paradise whom He wills, and guides to it whom He wills. ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾, that is, none but Him alone knows the number of His creation and the quantity of their hosts, of the angels and others, and no one is able to know that.

Ata' said: He means among the angels whom He created to punish the people of the Fire; none knows their number except Allah.

The meaning is: although the guardians of the Fire are nineteen, they have helpers and hosts of angels that no one knows except Allah, glorified is He.

Then He, glorified is He, returned to the mention of Saqar, and said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to mankind﴾. That is: Saqar, and what has been mentioned of the number of its guardians, is nothing but a reminder and an admonition to the world. It was also said: "And it" means the proofs, the arguments and the Qur'an, which are nothing but a reminder to mankind.

Al-Zajjaj said: The fire of this world is a reminder of the fire of the Hereafter, but this is far-fetched.

It was also said: "it", that is, the number of the guardians of Hell, is nothing but a reminder to mankind, so that they may know the perfection of Allah's power and that He has no need of helpers or supporters. It was also said that the pronoun in ﴿And it is not﴾ refers to the hosts.

Then, glorified is He, rebuked and restrained the deniers, and said: ﴿No! By the moon﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kalla" is a particle (silah) for the oath; the estimate is: "Nay, by the moon." It was also said that the meaning is: "Truly, by the moon."

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is a rejection of the claim of one who claims that he can contend with the guardians of Hell; that is, the matter is not as he says. Then He swore by the moon and what follows it, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.

﴿And by the night when it turns back﴾, that is, when it departs.

The majority read "idha" with an alif, and "dabara" in the pattern of "daraba", as an adverb of future time. Nafi', Hafs and Hamza read "idh" without alif, "adbara" in the pattern of "akrama", as an adverb of past time. "Dabara" and "adbara" are two dialects, just as one says "aqbala al-zaman" and "qabala al-zaman". One says "dabara al-layl" and "adbara" when it departs and goes away.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, that is, when it shines and becomes clear.

﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (al-kubar)﴾. This is the answer to the oath, and the pronoun refers to Saqar: that is, indeed Saqar is one of the great calamities or afflictions. "Al-kubar" and "al-kibar" are the plural of "kubra". Muqatil said: "al-kubar" is one of the names of the Fire. It was also said: indeed, their denial of Muhammad is one of the greatest things; and it was said that the rising of the Hour is one of the greatest things. From this is the poet's saying:

"O son of al-Mu'alla, one of the great calamities has descended,
the calamity of the age and the deaf one of the changes."

The majority read ﴿la-iḥda﴾ with a hamzah. Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn Kathir in one narration from him read "innaha hidá" without a hamzah.

Al-Kalbi said: By "al-kubar" he meant the levels (darakat) of Hell and its gates.

﴿A warner to mankind﴾. The accusative of "nadhiran" is a circumstantial state (hal) from the pronoun in "innaha", as said by al-Zajjaj.

It is related from him, and from al-Kisa'i and Abu Ali al-Farisi, that it is a state from His words ﴿Arise and warn﴾, that is: Arise, O Muhammad, and warn, as a warner to mankind.

Al-Farra' said: It is a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of warning, put in the accusative by an omitted verb.

It was also said that it is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz) for "ihda", because it includes the sense of magnification, as if it were said: "the greatest of the great ones in warning." It was also said that it is a verbal noun in the accusative governed by "anzara" mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "a'ni" (I mean). It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "ud'u" (call). It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "nadi" or "balligh" (proclaim).

It was also said that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), and the estimate is: "And indeed it is one of the greatest for the sake of warning mankind."

The majority read it in the accusative. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Abi Ablah read it in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning: "it is a warner" or "he is a warner."

There has been disagreement about the warner. Al-Hasan said: it is the Fire. It was said: (p-1555) Muhammad (ﷺ). Abu Razin said: the meaning is "I am a warner to you from it." It was said: the Qur'an is a warner to mankind because of what it contains of promise and threat.

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾. This is a substitute (badal) for His words "to mankind": that is, a warner to whoever among you wills to advance toward obedience or to hold back from it. The meaning is that the warning has reached everyone, both those who believed and those who disbelieved. It was said that the agent of the willing is Allah, glorified is He: that is, for whomever Allah wills among you to advance by faith or to lag behind by disbelief. The first is preferable.

As-Suddi said: for whoever among you wills to advance to the Fire, which was mentioned before, or to lag behind to Paradise.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas that he said: When Abu Jahl heard ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾, he said to Quraysh: "May your mothers be bereaved! Do I hear Ibn Abi Kabsha tell you that the guardians of Hell are nineteen, while you are the numerous ones? Would every ten of you be unable to overpower one man of the guardians of Hell?" Ibn Mardawayh also related from him, concerning His words ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved﴾, he said: Abu al-Ashadd said: "Leave me and the guardians of Hell; I will suffice you their burden." He said: "I have been told that the Prophet (ﷺ) described the guardians of Hell and said: 'As if their eyes were lightning, and as if their mouths were the horns of the wild cattle, dragging their hair. They have the strength of both humans and jinn. One of them will approach a nation of people, driving them, with a mountain on his neck, until he throws them into the Fire, and then he throws the mountain upon them.'"

At-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey, saying: "I and Jibril ascended to the lowest heaven, and there I saw an angel called Isma'il, who is the keeper of the lowest heaven, and before him were seventy thousand angels, with each angel having his host of one hundred thousand." And he recited this verse: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾.

Ahmad related from Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a space the size of a finger in it except that there is an angel prostrating upon it."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah.

Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib, and it is narrated from Abu Dharr as a mawquf (a statement of a companion).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿when it turns back﴾, that he said: "It is the turning back of its darkness."

Musaddad in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His words ﴿And by the night when it turns back﴾, and he remained silent with me until, at the end of the night, he heard the call to prayer, then he called to me: "O Mujahid, this is the time when the night has turned back."

Ibn Jarir related from him, concerning His words ﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾, that he said: "Whoever wills follows the obedience of Allah, and whoever wills lags behind from it."

It is related from him, and from al-Kisa'i and Abu Ali al-Farisi, that it is a state from His words ﴿Arise and warn﴾, that is: Arise, O Muhammad, and warn, as a warner to mankind.

Al-Farra' said: It is a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of warning, put in the accusative by an omitted verb.

It was also said that it is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz) for "ihda", because it includes the sense of magnification, as if it were said: "the greatest of the great ones in warning." It was also said that it is a verbal noun in the accusative governed by "anzara" mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "a'ni" (I mean). It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "ud'u" (call). It was said it is in the accusative by the implied "nadi" or "balligh" (proclaim).

It was also said that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), and the estimate is: "And indeed it is one of the greatest for the sake of warning mankind."

The majority read it in the accusative. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Abi Ablah read it in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning: "it is a warner" or "he is a warner."

There has been disagreement about the warner. Al-Hasan said: it is the Fire. It was said: (p-1555) Muhammad (ﷺ). Abu Razin said: the meaning is "I am a warner to you from it." It was said: the Qur'an is a warner to mankind because of what it contains of promise and threat.

﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾. This is a substitute (badal) for His words "to mankind": that is, a warner to whoever among you wills to advance toward obedience or to hold back from it. The meaning is that the warning has reached everyone, both those who believed and those who disbelieved. It was said that the agent of the willing is Allah, glorified is He: that is, for whomever Allah wills among you to advance by faith or to lag behind by disbelief. The first is preferable.

As-Suddi said: for whoever among you wills to advance to the Fire, which was mentioned before, or to lag behind to Paradise.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas that he said: When Abu Jahl heard ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾, he said to Quraysh: "May your mothers be bereaved! Do I hear Ibn Abi Kabsha tell you that the guardians of Hell are nineteen, while you are the numerous ones? Would every ten of you be unable to overpower one man of the guardians of Hell?" Ibn Mardawayh also related from him, concerning His words ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved﴾, he said: Abu al-Ashadd said: "Leave me and the guardians of Hell; I will suffice you their burden." He said: "I have been told that the Prophet (ﷺ) described the guardians of Hell and said: 'As if their eyes were lightning, and as if their mouths were the horns of the wild cattle, dragging their hair. They have the strength of both humans and jinn. One of them will approach a nation of people, driving them, with a mountain on his neck, until he throws them into the Fire, and then he throws the mountain upon them.'"

At-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Abu al-Shaykh related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey, saying: "I and Jibril ascended to the lowest heaven, and there I saw an angel called Isma'il, who is the keeper of the lowest heaven, and before him were seventy thousand angels, with each angel having his host of one hundred thousand." And he recited this verse: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾.

Ahmad related from Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a space the size of a finger in it except that there is an angel prostrating upon it."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah.

Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib, and it is narrated from Abu Dharr as a mawquf (a statement of a companion).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿when it turns back﴾, that he said: "It is the turning back of its darkness."

Musaddad in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His words ﴿And by the night when it turns back﴾, and he remained silent with me until, at the end of the night, he heard the call to prayer, then he called to me: "O Mujahid, this is the time when the night has turned back."

Ibn Jarir related from him, concerning His words ﴿For whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾, that he said: "Whoever wills follows the obedience of Allah, and whoever wills lags behind from it."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 74, verses 31–37:

When the words of the Most High were revealed, ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾, Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad have no helpers except nineteen? Muhammad frightens you with nineteen, while you are the numerous ones (al-duhm). Would each hundred men among you be unable to overpower one of them and then get out of the Fire?" Then Abu al-Ashadd, a man of the Banu Jumah, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, when the Day of Resurrection comes, I will walk in front of you and push ten of them with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and then we will go on and enter Paradise." So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, meaning: We have not made those who manage the affairs of the Fire and who carry out the punishment of its inhabitants anything except angels (p-1554). So who can withstand the angels, and who can overpower them? How, then, do you disbelievers attempt to contend with them?

It was also said that He made them angels because they are of a different kind from the created beings of jinn and humans, so they are not affected by the tenderness and compassion that affect gatherings of people. And it was said that it is because they are the most upright of God's creation in His right and in being angry for Him, and the strongest of them in might and the most powerful in seizing. ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial﴾, that is, a misguidance for those who considered their number small, and a tribulation for them. The meaning is: We have not made their number this number mentioned in the Qur'an except as a misguidance and a tribulation for them, so that they said what they said, in order that their punishment would be doubled and God's anger against them would increase.

It was also said that the meaning of ﴿except as a trial﴾ is except as a punishment, as in His words: ﴿On the Day they will be burned over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], that is, they will be punished. The lam in His words ﴿that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾ is connected to "We made". By "the People of the Scripture" is meant the Jews and the Christians, because what was revealed in the Qur'an agrees with what is in their possession, namely that the number of the guardians of Hell is nineteen. This was said by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Mujahid and others. The meaning is that Allah made the number of the guardians this number so that certainty would be attained by the Jews and the Christians regarding the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), because the Qur'an agrees with what is in their books. ﴿And those who believed may increase in faith﴾. It was said that by "those who believed" is meant those among the People of the Scripture who believed, such as Abd Allah ibn Salam. It was also said that he meant by "those who believed" the believers of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The meaning is: that they may increase in certainty upon their certainty, when they saw the agreement of the People of the Scripture with them. The clause ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾ confirms what preceded concerning certainty and the increase of faith. The meaning is the negation of doubt about them in the religion, or about the fact that the number of the guardians of Hell is nineteen. In reality there is no doubt among the believers, but this is by way of indirect address to others, those in whose hearts there is doubt. ﴿And so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ By "those in whose hearts is disease" are meant the hypocrites. Although the surah is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy at that time, this is a report of what would happen in Medina. Or the disease means merely the occurrence of doubt and uncertainty, which exists among the disbelievers.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, so the disease in this verse is the disagreement. By "and the disbelievers" is meant the disbelievers of the Arabs from the people of Mecca and others. The meaning of ﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾ is: what did He intend by this astonishing number, being astonishing like a parable.

Al-Layth said: "Mathal" means a statement (hadith), and from it is His word: ﴿The example of Paradise which the God-fearing have been promised﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35], that is, its description is the report about it. ﴿Thus Allah leaves astray whom He wills﴾, that is, like that misguidance mentioned before, which is His word: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieved﴾. ﴿Allah leaves astray whom He wills﴾ from among His servants. The kaf is an adjective (na't) of an omitted verbal noun (masdar). ﴿And guides whom He wills﴾ from among His servants. The meaning is: like that misguidance for the disbelievers and that guidance for the believers, Allah leaves astray whom He wills to be misguided and guides whom He wills to be guided.

It was also said that the meaning is: thus Allah leaves astray from Paradise whom He wills, and guides to it whom He wills. ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾, that is, none but Him alone knows the number of His creation and the quantity of their hosts, of the angels and others, and no one is able to know that.

Ata' said: He means among the angels whom He created to punish the people of the Fire; none knows their number except Allah.

The meaning is: although the guardians of the Fire are nineteen, they have helpers and hosts of angels that no one knows except Allah, glorified is He.

Then He, glorified is He, returned to the mention of Saqar, and said: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to mankind﴾. That is: Saqar, and what has been mentioned of the number of its guardians, is nothing but a reminder and an admonition to the world. It was also said: "And it" means the proofs, the arguments and the Qur'an, which are nothing but a reminder to mankind.

Al-Zajjaj said: The fire of this world is a reminder of the fire of the Hereafter, but this is far-fetched.

It was also said: "it", that is, the number of the guardians of Hell, is nothing but a reminder to mankind, so that they may know the perfection of Allah's power and that He has no need of helpers or supporters. It was also said that the pronoun in ﴿And it is not﴾ refers to the hosts.

Then, glorified is He, rebuked and restrained the deniers, and said: ﴿No! By the moon﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kalla" is a particle (silah) for the oath; the estimate is: "Nay, by the moon." It was also said that the meaning is: "Truly, by the moon."

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is a rejection of the claim of one who claims that he can contend with the guardians of Hell; that is, the matter is not as he says. Then He swore by the moon and what follows it, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.

﴿And by the night when it turns back﴾, that is, when it departs.

The majority read "idha" with an alif, and "dabara" in the pattern of "daraba", as an adverb of future time. Nafi', Hafs and Hamza read "idh" without alif, "adbara" in the pattern of "akrama", as an adverb of past time. "Dabara" and "adbara" are two dialects, just as one says "aqbala al-zaman" and "qabala al-zaman". One says "dabara al-layl" and "adbara" when it departs and goes away.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, that is, when it shines and becomes clear.

﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (al-kubar)﴾. This is the answer to the oath, and the pronoun refers to Saqar: that is, indeed Saqar is one of the great calamities or afflictions. "Al-kubar" and "al-kibar" are the plural of "kubra". Muqatil said: "al-kubar" is one of the names of the Fire. It was also said: indeed, their denial of Muhammad is one of the greatest things; and it was said that the rising of the Hour is one of the greatest things. From this is the poet's saying:

"O son of al-Mu'alla, one of the great calamities has descended,
the calamity of the age and the deaf one of the changes."

The majority read ﴿la-iḥda﴾ with a hamzah. Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn Kathir in one narration from him read "innaha hidá" without a hamzah.

Al-Kalbi said: By "al-kubar" he meant the levels (darakat) of Hell and its gates.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 74, verses 38–56:

His saying: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ means: taken to account for its deeds and held in pledge by them, either it frees itself or it destroys itself. Al-rahina (the pledge) is a noun in the sense of al-rahn (the pledge), like al-shima (disposition) in the sense of al-shiyam (dispositions), and it is not an adjective. Had it been an adjective, it would have been said "rahin," because fa'il takes the same form for the masculine and the feminine. The meaning is: every soul is a pledge for its earning, not released.

﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾: they are not held in pledge by their sins, but release themselves by the good deeds they have done.

Their identity has been disputed. It is said they are the angels; it is said they are the believers; it is said they are the children of the Muslims; it is said they are those who were on the right of Adam; it is said they are the people of truth; it is said they are those who rely on grace rather than deeds; and it is said they are those whom Allah has chosen for His service.

﴿In gardens﴾: it is in a position of nominative case, as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is a resumptive answer to a question arising from what precedes. It may also be that ﴿in gardens﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (hal) of "the companions of the right hand," or a circumstantial phrase of the subject of ﴿they will ask one another﴾, or an adverbial of time/place for ﴿they will ask one another﴾. His saying ﴿they will ask one another﴾ may be in its original sense: that is, some of them ask others. It may also be in the sense of ﴿they will ask﴾: that is, they ask others, as in "da'iyyatihi" and "tada'iyyatihi." On the first interpretation,

﴿concerning the criminals﴾ is connected to ﴿they will ask one another﴾: that is, some ask others about the condition of the criminals. On the second interpretation, "'an" is superfluous: that is, they ask the criminals.

His saying ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ is under an implied "say": that is, they ask one another concerning the criminals, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾; or they ask them, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾. The sentence, on both interpretations, is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and the meaning is: what caused you to enter Saqar? One says "salaktu al-khayta fi kadha" (I threaded the thread into such-and-such) when one makes it enter it.

Al-Kalbi said: a man from the people of Paradise asks a man from the people of the Fire by his name, and says to him: "O so-and-so, what has brought you into the Fire?"

It is said that they ask the angels about their relatives, and the angels ask the polytheists, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾

Al-Farra' said: in this there is what strengthens the view that the companions of the right hand are the children, because they do not know sins.

﴿They will say: We were not among those who prayed﴾: that is, among the believers who prayed to Allah in the world.

﴿Nor were we feeding the poor﴾: that is, we did not give charity to the needy. It is said that these two are to be understood as the obligatory prayer and the obligatory charity, since there is no punishment for what is not obligatory; and in this there is evidence that the disbelievers are addressed concerning the legal obligations.

﴿And we used to plunge with the plungers﴾: that is, we mixed with the people of falsehood in their falsehood.

Qatadah said: whenever a misguided one went astray, we went astray with him.

Al-Suddi said: we used to deny together with the deniers.

Ibn Zayd said: we plunged with the plungers concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and this was their saying: "a liar, a madman, a sorcerer, a poet."

﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾: that is, the Day of Recompense and Reckoning.

﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾: and this is death, as in His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ [al-Hijr: 99].

﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾: that is, the intercession of the angels and the prophets, as it benefits the righteous.

﴿Then what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ Al-tadhkira (the reminder) is the admonition by the admonitions of the Qur'an. The fa' (then) is for establishing, as a consequence of what precedes, the denunciation of their turning away from the reminder, given the reasons that necessitate turning towards it. The accusative of "mu'ridin" is as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in the complement of the prepositional phrase: that is, what happened to them while they were turning away from the Qur'an, which contains the great reminder and the supreme admonition.

Then He compared them, in their aversion from the Qur'an, to donkeys, saying: ﴿As if they were frightened donkeys﴾. The sentence is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in "mu'ridin," by interlocution. The meaning of "mustanfirah" is fleeing (nafirah); it is said "nafara" and "istanfara," like "ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The intended meaning is the wild donkeys.

The majority read "mustanfirah" with a kasra on the fa': that is, fleeing. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with a fatha: that is, "munaffarah" (startled, panicked). Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the second reading.

In al-Kashshaf it says: "al-mustanfirah" is the very fleeing, as if it seeks flight from its own souls in gathering itself for it and driving itself towards it.

﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾: that is, from archers shooting at them. Al-qaswarah is the archer, and its plural is qaswarah; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Kaysan. It is said it is the lion, as said by 'Ata' and al-Kalbi.

Ibn 'Arafah said: it is from al-qasr in the sense of subduing, because it subdues the beasts. It is said al-qaswarah are the voices of people. It is said al-qaswarah in the language of the Arabs is the lion, and in the language of Abyssinia are the archers.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-qaswarah is the beginning of the night, that is: they fled from the darkness of the night; and 'Ikrimah said likewise. The first view is preferable. Every strong thing in the eyes of the Arabs is a qaswarah, and from this is the saying of the poet:

O daughter, be a good choice for her goodness; her maternal kin are the tribe and the people of al-qaswarah.

And from it is the saying of Labid:

When we call a cry in our assembly, the men come to us, the worshipful, the qasawir.

And from its application to the lion is the saying of the poet:

A hidden one whom the heroes fear, as if he were the qaswar al-rahhal.

﴿Rather, each one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾: it is a conjunction to an omitted element required by the context, as if it were said: they are not satisfied with that reminder, but rather each one of them desires...

The exegetes said: the disbelievers of Quraysh said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "Let there be at the head of each of us a written scroll from Allah that you are the Messenger of Allah."

The suhuf are books, singular sahifah; and al-munashsharah is the spread-out, the opened. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Until you cause to descend upon us a book that we may read﴾ [al-Isra': 93]. The majority read "munashsharah" with doubling (tashdid). Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it without doubling.

The majority also read "suhuf" with a damma on the ha'. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it with sukun.

Then Allah, glorified is He, rebuked them and repelled them from this saying, saying: ﴿No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾: meaning the punishment of the Hereafter, for if they feared the Fire they would not have demanded signs. It is said that "kalla" here means "truly."

Then He repeated the repelling and rebuke to them, saying: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾: meaning the Qur'an; or, truly, indeed it is a reminder. The meaning is that one is reminded by it and admonished by its exhortations.

﴿So whoever wills, will remember it﴾: that is, whoever wills to be admonished by it is admonished.

Then He, glorified is He, returned the will to Himself, saying: ﴿But they will not remember except that Allah wills﴾. The majority read "yadhkurun" with the ya' (third person). Nafi' and Ya'qub read it with the ta' (second person). They agreed on the light (non-doubled) form. The phrase ﴿except that Allah wills﴾ is an exceptive construction from the most general of circumstances.

Muqatil said: "except that Allah wills guidance for them." ﴿He is worthy of piety﴾: that is, He is worthy that the pious should fear Him by abandoning His disobedience and acting by His obedience. ﴿And worthy of forgiveness﴾: that is, He is worthy to forgive the believers whatever sins have passed from them, and worthy to accept the repentance of the penitent among the sinners, and so forgive their sins.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ that he said: "taken to account for its deeds."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him concerning His saying ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾ that he said: "they are the Muslims."

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾ that he said: "they are the children of the Muslims."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾ that he said: "death."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari concerning His saying ﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾ that he said: "they are the archers, the men of the bows."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "al-qaswarah: the men who are archers, the hunters."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Jamrah that he said: "I said to Ibn 'Abbas: 'Is al-qaswarah the lion?' He said: 'I do not know it in the language of any of the Arabs as the lion; they are a band of men.'"

Al-rahina (the pledge) is a noun in the sense of al-rahn (the pledge), like al-shima (disposition) in the sense of al-shiyam (dispositions), and it is not an adjective. Had it been an adjective, it would have been said "rahin," because fa'il takes the same form for the masculine and the feminine. The meaning is: every soul is a pledge for its earning, not released.

﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾: they are not held in pledge by their sins, but release themselves by the good deeds they have done.

Their identity has been disputed. It is said they are the angels; it is said they are the believers; it is said they are the children of the Muslims; it is said they are those who were on the right of Adam; it is said they are the people of truth; it is said they are those who rely on grace rather than deeds; and it is said they are those whom Allah has chosen for His service.

﴿In gardens﴾: it is in a position of nominative case, as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is a resumptive answer to a question arising from what precedes. It may also be that ﴿in gardens﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (hal) of "the companions of the right hand," or a circumstantial phrase of the subject of ﴿they will ask one another﴾, or an adverbial of time/place for ﴿they will ask one another﴾. His saying ﴿they will ask one another﴾ may be in its original sense: that is, some of them ask others. It may also be in the sense of ﴿they will ask﴾: that is, they ask others, as in "da'iyyatihi" and "tada'iyyatihi." On the first interpretation,

﴿concerning the criminals﴾ is connected to ﴿they will ask one another﴾: that is, some ask others about the condition of the criminals. On the second interpretation, "'an" is superfluous: that is, they ask the criminals.

His saying ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ is under an implied "say": that is, they ask one another concerning the criminals, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾; or they ask them, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾. The sentence, on both interpretations, is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and the meaning is: what caused you to enter Saqar? One says "salaktu al-khayta fi kadha" (I threaded the thread into such-and-such) when one makes it enter it.

Al-Kalbi said: a man from the people of Paradise asks a man from the people of the Fire by his name, and says to him: "O so-and-so, what has brought you into the Fire?"

It is said that they ask the angels about their relatives, and the angels ask the polytheists, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾

Al-Farra' said: in this there is what strengthens the view that the companions of the right hand are the children, because they do not know sins.

﴿They will say: We were not among those who prayed﴾: that is, among the believers who prayed to Allah in the world.

﴿Nor were we feeding the poor﴾: that is, we did not give charity to the needy. It is said that these two are to be understood as the obligatory prayer and the obligatory charity, since there is no punishment for what is not obligatory; and in this there is evidence that the disbelievers are addressed concerning the legal obligations.

﴿And we used to plunge with the plungers﴾: that is, we mixed with the people of falsehood in their falsehood.

Qatadah said: whenever a misguided one went astray, we went astray with him.

Al-Suddi said: we used to deny together with the deniers.

Ibn Zayd said: we plunged with the plungers concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and this was their saying: "a liar, a madman, a sorcerer, a poet."

﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾: that is, the Day of Recompense and Reckoning.

﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾: and this is death, as in His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ [al-Hijr: 99].

﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾: that is, the intercession of the angels and the prophets, as it benefits the righteous.

﴿Then what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ Al-tadhkira (the reminder) is the admonition by the admonitions of the Qur'an. The fa' (then) is for establishing, as a consequence of what precedes, the denunciation of their turning away from the reminder, given the reasons that necessitate turning towards it. The accusative of "mu'ridin" is as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in the complement of the prepositional phrase: that is, what happened to them while they were turning away from the Qur'an, which contains the great reminder and the supreme admonition.

Then He compared them, in their aversion from the Qur'an, to donkeys, saying: ﴿As if they were frightened donkeys﴾. The sentence is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in "mu'ridin," by interlocution. The meaning of "mustanfirah" is fleeing (nafirah); it is said "nafara" and "istanfara," like "ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The intended meaning is the wild donkeys.

The majority read "mustanfirah" with a kasra on the fa': that is, fleeing. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with a fatha: that is, "munaffarah" (startled, panicked). Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the second reading.

In al-Kashshaf it says: "al-mustanfirah" is the very fleeing, as if it seeks flight from its own souls in gathering itself for it and driving itself towards it.

﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾: that is, from archers shooting at them. Al-qaswarah is the archer, and its plural is qaswarah; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Kaysan. It is said it is the lion, as said by 'Ata' and al-Kalbi.

Ibn 'Arafah said: it is from al-qasr in the sense of subduing, because it subdues the beasts. It is said al-qaswarah are the voices of people. It is said al-qaswarah in the language of the Arabs is the lion, and in the language of Abyssinia are the archers.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-qaswarah is the beginning of the night, that is: they fled from the darkness of the night; and 'Ikrimah said likewise. The first view is preferable. Every strong thing in the eyes of the Arabs is a qaswarah, and from this is the saying of the poet:

O daughter, be a good choice for her goodness; her maternal kin are the tribe and the people of al-qaswarah.

And from it is the saying of Labid:

When we call a cry in our assembly, the men come to us, the worshipful, the qasawir.

And from its application to the lion is the saying of the poet:

A hidden one whom the heroes fear, as if he were the qaswar al-rahhal.

﴿Rather, each one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾: it is a conjunction to an omitted element required by the context, as if it were said: they are not satisfied with that reminder, but rather each one of them desires...

The exegetes said: the disbelievers of Quraysh said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "Let there be at the head of each of us a written scroll from Allah that you are the Messenger of Allah."

The suhuf are books, singular sahifah; and al-munashsharah is the spread-out, the opened. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Until you cause to descend upon us a book that we may read﴾ [al-Isra': 93]. The majority read "munashsharah" with doubling (tashdid). Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it without doubling.

The majority also read "suhuf" with a damma on the ha'. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it with sukun.

Then Allah, glorified is He, rebuked them and repelled them from this saying, saying: ﴿No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾: meaning the punishment of the Hereafter, for if they feared the Fire they would not have demanded signs. It is said that "kalla" here means "truly."

Then He repeated the repelling and rebuke to them, saying: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾: meaning the Qur'an; or, truly, indeed it is a reminder. The meaning is that one is reminded by it and admonished by its exhortations.

﴿So whoever wills, will remember it﴾: that is, whoever wills to be admonished by it is admonished.

Then He, glorified is He, returned the will to Himself, saying: ﴿But they will not remember except that Allah wills﴾. The majority read "yadhkurun" with the ya' (third person). Nafi' and Ya'qub read it with the ta' (second person). They agreed on the light (non-doubled) form. The phrase ﴿except that Allah wills﴾ is an exceptive construction from the most general of circumstances.

Muqatil said: "except that Allah wills guidance for them." ﴿He is worthy of piety﴾: that is, He is worthy that the pious should fear Him by abandoning His disobedience and acting by His obedience. ﴿And worthy of forgiveness﴾: that is, He is worthy to forgive the believers whatever sins have passed from them, and worthy to accept the repentance of the penitent among the sinners, and so forgive their sins.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ that he said: "taken to account for its deeds."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him concerning His saying ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾ that he said: "they are the Muslims."

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾ that he said: "they are the children of the Muslims."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾ that he said: "death."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari concerning His saying ﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾ that he said: "they are the archers, the men of the bows."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "al-qaswarah: the men who are archers, the hunters."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Jamrah that he said: "I said to Ibn 'Abbas: 'Is al-qaswarah the lion?' He said: 'I do not know it in the language of any of the Arabs as the lion; they are a band of men.'"

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, 'Abd al-Razzaq, and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿from a lion﴾ that he said: "it is the noise of people: meaning their voices."

Ahmad, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn 'Adi, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh related from Anas that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾ and said: 'Your Lord said: I am worthy that I be feared, so no god is made with Me; so whoever fears Me and does not make a god with Me, I am worthy to forgive him.'"

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Umar, and Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 74, verses 38–56:

His saying: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ means: taken to account for its deeds and held in pledge by them, either it frees itself or it destroys itself. Al-rahina (the pledge) is a noun in the sense of al-rahn (the pledge), like al-shima (disposition) in the sense of al-shiyam (dispositions), and it is not an adjective. Had it been an adjective, it would have been said "rahin," because fa'il takes the same form for the masculine and the feminine. The meaning is: every soul is a pledge for its earning, not released.

﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾: they are not held in pledge by their sins, but release themselves by the good deeds they have done.

Their identity has been disputed. It is said they are the angels; it is said they are the believers; it is said they are the children of the Muslims; it is said they are those who were on the right of Adam; it is said they are the people of truth; it is said they are those who rely on grace rather than deeds; and it is said they are those whom Allah has chosen for His service.

﴿In gardens﴾: it is in a position of nominative case, as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is a resumptive answer to a question arising from what precedes. It may also be that ﴿in gardens﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (hal) of "the companions of the right hand," or a circumstantial phrase of the subject of ﴿they will ask one another﴾, or an adverbial of time/place for ﴿they will ask one another﴾. His saying ﴿they will ask one another﴾ may be in its original sense: that is, some of them ask others. It may also be in the sense of ﴿they will ask﴾: that is, they ask others, as in "da'iyyatihi" and "tada'iyyatihi." On the first interpretation,

﴿concerning the criminals﴾ is connected to ﴿they will ask one another﴾: that is, some ask others about the condition of the criminals. On the second interpretation, "'an" is superfluous: that is, they ask the criminals.

His saying ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ is under an implied "say": that is, they ask one another concerning the criminals, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾; or they ask them, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾. The sentence, on both interpretations, is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and the meaning is: what caused you to enter Saqar? One says "salaktu al-khayta fi kadha" (I threaded the thread into such-and-such) when one makes it enter it.

Al-Kalbi said: a man from the people of Paradise asks a man from the people of the Fire by his name, and says to him: "O so-and-so, what has brought you into the Fire?"

It is said that they ask the angels about their relatives, and the angels ask the polytheists, saying to them: ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾

Al-Farra' said: in this there is what strengthens the view that the companions of the right hand are the children, because they do not know sins.

﴿They will say: We were not among those who prayed﴾: that is, among the believers who prayed to Allah in the world.

﴿Nor were we feeding the poor﴾: that is, we did not give charity to the needy. It is said that these two are to be understood as the obligatory prayer and the obligatory charity, since there is no punishment for what is not obligatory; and in this there is evidence that the disbelievers are addressed concerning the legal obligations.

﴿And we used to plunge with the plungers﴾: that is, we mixed with the people of falsehood in their falsehood.

Qatadah said: whenever a misguided one went astray, we went astray with him.

Al-Suddi said: we used to deny together with the deniers.

Ibn Zayd said: we plunged with the plungers concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and this was their saying: "a liar, a madman, a sorcerer, a poet."

﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾: that is, the Day of Recompense and Reckoning.

﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾: and this is death, as in His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ [al-Hijr: 99].

﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾: that is, the intercession of the angels and the prophets, as it benefits the righteous.

﴿Then what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ Al-tadhkira (the reminder) is the admonition by the admonitions of the Qur'an. The fa' (then) is for establishing, as a consequence of what precedes, the denunciation of their turning away from the reminder, given the reasons that necessitate turning towards it. The accusative of "mu'ridin" is as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in the complement of the prepositional phrase: that is, what happened to them while they were turning away from the Qur'an, which contains the great reminder and the supreme admonition.

Then He compared them, in their aversion from the Qur'an, to donkeys, saying: ﴿As if they were frightened donkeys﴾. The sentence is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in "mu'ridin," by interlocution. The meaning of "mustanfirah" is fleeing (nafirah); it is said "nafara" and "istanfara," like "ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The intended meaning is the wild donkeys.

The majority read "mustanfirah" with a kasra on the fa': that is, fleeing. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with a fatha: that is, "munaffarah" (startled, panicked). Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the second reading.

In al-Kashshaf it says: "al-mustanfirah" is the very fleeing, as if it seeks flight from its own souls in gathering itself for it and driving itself towards it.

﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾: that is, from archers shooting at them. Al-qaswarah is the archer, and its plural is qaswarah; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Kaysan. It is said it is the lion, as said by 'Ata' and al-Kalbi.

Ibn 'Arafah said: it is from al-qasr in the sense of subduing, because it subdues the beasts. It is said al-qaswarah are the voices of people. It is said al-qaswarah in the language of the Arabs is the lion, and in the language of Abyssinia are the archers.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-qaswarah is the beginning of the night, that is: they fled from the darkness of the night; and 'Ikrimah said likewise. The first view is preferable. Every strong thing in the eyes of the Arabs is a qaswarah, and from this is the saying of the poet:

O daughter, be a good choice for her goodness; her maternal kin are the tribe and the people of al-qaswarah.

And from it is the saying of Labid:

When we call a cry in our assembly, the men come to us, the worshipful, the qasawir.

And from its application to the lion is the saying of the poet:

A hidden one whom the heroes fear, as if he were the qaswar al-rahhal.

﴿Rather, each one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾: it is a conjunction to an omitted element required by the context, as if it were said: they are not satisfied with that reminder, but rather each one of them desires...

The exegetes said: the disbelievers of Quraysh said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "Let there be at the head of each of us a written scroll from Allah that you are the Messenger of Allah."

The suhuf are books, singular sahifah; and al-munashsharah is the spread-out, the opened. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Until you cause to descend upon us a book that we may read﴾ [al-Isra': 93]. The majority read "munashsharah" with doubling (tashdid). Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it without doubling.

The majority also read "suhuf" with a damma on the ha'. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read it with sukun.

Then Allah, glorified is He, rebuked them and repelled them from this saying, saying: ﴿No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾: meaning the punishment of the Hereafter, for if they feared the Fire they would not have demanded signs. It is said that "kalla" here means "truly."

Then He repeated the repelling and rebuke to them, saying: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾: meaning the Qur'an; or, truly, indeed it is a reminder. The meaning is that one is reminded by it and admonished by its exhortations.

﴿So whoever wills, will remember it﴾: that is, whoever wills to be admonished by it is admonished.

Then He, glorified is He, returned the will to Himself, saying: ﴿But they will not remember except that Allah wills﴾. The majority read "yadhkurun" with the ya' (third person). Nafi' and Ya'qub read it with the ta' (second person). They agreed on the light (non-doubled) form. The phrase ﴿except that Allah wills﴾ is an exceptive construction from the most general of circumstances.

Muqatil said: "except that Allah wills guidance for them." ﴿He is worthy of piety﴾: that is, He is worthy that the pious should fear Him by abandoning His disobedience and acting by His obedience. ﴿And worthy of forgiveness﴾: that is, He is worthy to forgive the believers whatever sins have passed from them, and worthy to accept the repentance of the penitent among the sinners, and so forgive their sins.
